evidence: A screen on committed products and cited values. The natural night is the calendar's evaluator on its transfer product in the mean geometry (clear sky, level ground, no libration, refraction, terrain, cloud or haze), reproducing the provisioning branch's daily-life calendars and main's per-place Earthlight. Living light is measured photon outputs and quantum yields from the literature, turned into luminance and path light by CIE photometry with Gaussian stand-ins for the emission spectra, and costed from each luciferin cycle's stoichiometry at Hinkle's P/O ratios, without the cost of making the enzymes. Needs are Earth lighting standards and experiments. Skyglow is a single-scattering model of a uniform disk town in the Moon's and Earth's air, calibrated on ecology's Earth-statistics areas a person; multiple scattering, spectra, towns' shapes and their overlaps are not modelled. No organism, lamp or town here exists or has been tested.
reading_rule: Light is lux on level ground and cd/m2 for surfaces (photopic unless named scotopic). Hours are per 708.73-hour cycle. [low, high] pairs bound each quantity over the ranges named in design_guesses and in the cited values. emitters.organisms gives each luminous organism's or engineered plant's light and its cost through a 354-hour night; emitters.targets the glow and the cost a closed glowing canopy needs for each need on the path below it; emitters.limits the path light a share of the night store buys. needs gives, per place and per ways-of-living home, the hours below each need's level and the lamp light lacking at the darkest moment. skyglow gives the area a person under a light-polluted sky at the night's darkest moment by home and design, in m2, and the share of the dry land by provisioning's mixes at 4, 6 and 8 billion lunar residents, all on the land or half aloft. Values computed here are screen values; arithmetic on cited values is derived; design guesses are ranges.

orientation.task: moving about open ground by eye, as under a summer full moon on Earth
orientation.basis: full moonlight on Earth is typically 0.05-0.1 lux in temperate summers, 0.05-0.2 lux at most full moons and at most about 0.3 lux (Kyba, Mohar & Posch 2017)

colour.basis: paper samples were sorted into their colour groups above 0.32 lux; at 0.1-0.01 lux only reds and oranges were named reliably (Pokorny et al. 2006)

walking.basis: 1.0 lux lets pedestrians of all ages detect a 10-mm trip hazard under any lamp, 0.22-0.93 lux by lamp and age (Fotios & Uttley 2018); detection reaches its plateau at 2.0 lux (Uttley et al. 2017); the lowest pedestrian class, P6, asks 2.0 lux on average and 0.4 lux at least (CIE 115:2010, as Fotios & Gibbons 2018 tabulate it)

faces at 4 m.basis: semi-cylindrical illuminance of 0.8 lux at 4 m and 2.7 lux at 10 m (Caminada & van Bommel 1980, as Fotios, Yang & Cheal 2015 report it)

reading.basis: at a mesopic 2 cd/m2 people read at full speed with a larger critical print size (Penaloza et al. 2025): about 8 lux on paper of reflectance 0.8 (derived)

work.task: close work and reading small print outdoors
work.basis: 100 lux for reading addresses outdoors and 500 lux for reading and writing indoors (EN 12464-2 and EN 12464-1, as the Zumtobel lighting handbook reprints them)

checks_against_daily_life.note: largest deviation from the daily-life calendars beyond their printed precision (lux to 4 decimals, hours to 2)

fungal.note: HispS adenylates caffeic acid and adds two malonyl-CoA (two ATP at acetyl-CoA carboxylase, two more at ATP-citrate lyase for the cytosol's acetyl-CoA); H3H uses NADPH and O2, wasting 30% of the NADPH; Luz releases CO2 and light; CPH returns caffeic acid and pyruvate

firefly.note: luciferase spends ATP to AMP and pyrophosphate; oxyluciferin returns to luciferin through 2-cyano-6-hydroxybenzothiazole and one cysteine

bacterial.note: FMNH2 from NAD(P)H; the fatty acid back to aldehyde by LuxCDE with ATP to AMP and NADPH

fungal pathway.basis: Mycena luciferases with 3-hydroxyhispidin: 0.017 (gill) and 0.00096 (stipe), Teranishi 2018; the fungal quantum yield is not yet established (Kusuma et al. 2025)

firefly chemistry.basis: Photinus pyralis luciferase: 0.41 +/- 0.074 (Ando et al. 2008); 0.48 (Niwa et al. 2010, as Niwa et al. 2023 report)

bacterial chemistry.basis: 0.17 photons per aldehyde (Shimomura, Johnson & Kohama 1972); about 0.1-0.16 (Kaku et al. 2021, citing Hastings & Nealson 1977)

thermodynamic floor.basis: one photon per luciferin and nothing lost

no_claims: No organism, glowing plant, lamp or town named here exists or has been tested.
Need levels are Earth standards and experiments with people adapted to Earth's nights.
Skyglow areas are Falchi et al.'s astronomical measure carried to the Moon; ecological effects begin at other levels.
